questions.question: What problem does the KV cache solve during autoregressive inference?
options: Memory overflow from large models
Redundant recomputation of key and value matrices for all previous tokens at each generation step
Slow tokenization
High GPU utilization
questions.explanation: Without KV cache, generating token t requires recomputing K and V for all t-1 previous tokens. The KV cache stores computed K and V tensors, so each new step only computes K/V for the newest token and appends it — reducing generation from O(n²) to O(n) recomputation.

questions.question: What is the memory cost of the KV cache for a typical LLM?
options: Negligible — it reuses model weights
2 × n_layers × n_heads × seq_len × d_head × bytes_per_element (grows linearly with context length)
Fixed regardless of sequence length
Proportional to the number of output tokens only
questions.explanation: KV cache stores K and V for every layer and every token. For LLaMA-3 70B with 32K context in fp16: ~2 × 80 layers × 8 heads × 32K × 128 × 2 bytes ≈ 160 GB. KV cache memory is often the binding constraint for serving long-context models.

questions.question: What is the core optimization in Flash Attention?
options: Quantizing attention weights to INT8
Tiling the attention computation to avoid materializing the full n×n attention matrix in HBM, keeping intermediate results in fast SRAM
Pruning attention heads with low importance scores
Using sparse attention patterns
questions.explanation: Standard attention writes the full n×n softmax matrix to HBM (slow memory). Flash Attention tiles the computation: processes blocks that fit in SRAM (fast), computing softmax incrementally. Memory usage drops from O(n²) to O(n) and wall-clock time improves 2-4× despite same FLOP count.

questions.question: What is Grouped Query Attention (GQA) and which models use it?
options: Multiple query heads sharing a single key-value head group, reducing KV cache size — used in LLaMA-2/3, Mistral, Gemma
Grouping attention heads by query type for better specialization
Using separate attention for different input groups
A method for merging attention heads during fine-tuning
questions.explanation: GQA groups multiple query heads to share a single K/V head. With 8 query heads per KV group, KV cache shrinks 8× vs Multi-Head Attention with minimal quality loss. LLaMA-2/3, Mistral, and Gemma all use GQA to make large-context inference practical.

questions.question: What is speculative decoding and how does it use the KV cache?
options: A method to compress the KV cache
A small draft model generates k tokens quickly; the target model verifies all k in parallel — accepted tokens reuse the draft's KV cache
Running multiple beam search paths simultaneously
Pre-filling the KV cache with common phrases
questions.explanation: A small (fast) draft model proposes k tokens. The large target model evaluates all k in one forward pass (parallel verification). Accepted tokens are appended to the KV cache; rejected tokens are regenerated. This achieves 2-4× speedup because the target model runs fewer sequential steps.
